subject: What AWS instance tpe for shiny-server ?

messages.author: 1e1f6c27d3c442a5
messages.subject: What AWS instance tpe for shiny-server ?
parts:
Hi,

I try to deploy some shiny-server on an AWS instance, and the reactivity is quite bad. It is not very easy to trace the time spent in different tasks, so I wonder what kind of instance is recommended for such hosting ?

Especially, if someone from Rstudio can tell us what instance they use for your glimmer and spark servers... 

My shiny app is not to complicated, but calls some system(), so I also wonder if it could not be an issue for performance.

Best,

Yann

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: What AWS instance tpe for shiny-server ?
parts:
Hi Yann,

I'm not sure about the exact instance types for Spark/Glimmer, but I've been running a Shiny Server on an "m1.small x64" AWS instance with pretty good performance. (http://trestletechnology.net:3838/reactiveGeyeser/) After app startup time, the responsiveness seems to be pretty good (at least from the US, where the server is).

We are gradually working towards some features that would offer insight into the performance of Shiny apps, but we don't really have anything useful ready just yet. 

A couple of additional thoughts:
  1. I've heard that AWS instances can vary drastically in terms of their performance. Sometimes you'll get put on a box which is oversubscribed for CPU and/or bandwidth and your instance won't perform very well. The suggestion I've heard in such instances is to shut down the machine and bring up another one to try again.
  2. You could try loading some static assets form your apps to test the performance independent of any Shiny reactivity. For instance, I can open http://trestletechnology.net:3838/reactiveGeyeser/shared/bootstrap/css/bootstrap-responsive.min.css on my server with the network tab open in Google Chrome to see exactly how long it's taking to load a simple, static file. If it's taking a long time to open a small, static file on an otherwise idle server, that may indicate that your EC2 instance doesn't have the appropriate CPU or Bandwidth to be able to perform well. If that file does load quickly, that may indict the Shiny application's performance. If that were the case, it may be worthwhile to profile your Shiny app more closely to see where the slowdown might be.
Best,
Jeff
